name: A Letter from Chief Export Compliance Officer to Business Partners 2026Q2.pdf
text:
[p1]
Dear Business Partner,
ZTE believes that export compliance is of critical importance to the sustainable
development of our partnership. This newsletter outlines the major efforts we have made in
export control compliance in Q2 2026. We believe that these efforts will help manage
export control compliance risks and facilitate the sound development of our business
relationship.
Regarding policy monitoring and response, in Q2, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS)
of the U.S. Department of Commerce issued guidance regarding the enforcement of
license requirements for advanced computing items and relevant FAQs. These changes,
after assessment, have limited overall impact on the company. In addition, the U.S.
legislature is actively advancing several bills to tighten export controls on China.
Accordingly, the company will continue to monitor relevant legislative and regulatory
developments overseas.
At the same time, China successively issued regulations on industrial, supply chain
security, and rules on countermeasures against foreign states' unlawful extraterritorial
jurisdiction. Multiple entities from the U.S. and Japan were added to China's export control
list. The company has completed policy interpretation and impact assessment, and
implemented corresponding compliance measures to ensure compliant business
operations. In addition, in response to China's increasingly stringent customs regulations
on the export of dual-use items, the company strictly carried out various export
compliance management measures to maintain a solid compliance foundation for
business growth.
In Q2, our self-developed Enterprise Compliance Service System (ECSS) continued to gain
recognition from industry leaders. The company secured compliance digitalization projects
from well-known companies such as ANTA Sports, Voyah Automobile, LiuGong Machinery,
HİZMETE ÖZEL - INTERNAL

[p2]
Huayou Cobalt, and China Great Wall Industry, becoming a preferred partner for digital
compliance management among top-tier enterprises in China.
We also actively communicated our digital compliance management practices with
external partners. In June, the company was invited to a workshop in Guangxi on enhancing
trade compliance capabilities for enterprises with cross-border operations. During the
workshop, we shared the ECSS-enabled compliance digital solutions and our cross-
industry collaboration experience, contributing to more robust trade compliance practices.
Moreover, the company has further enhanced its compliance credibility. In Q2, I worked
with our compliance team to actively expand outreach to senior executives at multinational
banks, while sustaining compliance engagement with the senior management of telecom
operators. We systematically showcased our mature compliance management system and
ECSS-enabled digital compliance management, comprehensively demonstrating our
profound compliance expertise. Such exchanges have strengthened trust and recognition
from customers across governments, enterprises, and financial institutions at home and
abroad and laid a solid foundation for deep and long-term strategic collaboration built on
security and compliance.
We also made progress in strengthening our compliance system. Given the dynamic
changes in global export control policies, the company continued to iterate its compliance
rule system. In Q2, we revised the corporate-level and BU-level manuals for export control
compliance, and updated the relevant business control regulations. Moreover, efforts were
made to strengthen the visible control and dynamic early warning of cross-broader
compliance risks, with an aim to accurately identify compliance red flags and weak points
in business collaboration. Specifically, the company conducted a targeted assessment of
export control compliance red flags, and established an end-to-end compliance
management process covering policy benchmarking, risk identification, and closed-loop
control, providing a more stable, secure, and reliable environment for business partners.
Leveraging our continuously evolving compliance system and the self-developed ECSS
system, we offer standardized, intelligent, and end-to-end compliance solutions for
business partners to achieve digital compliance management and navigate risks in cross-
border operations. We look forward to collaborating with partners across industries to build
a compliant, resilient, and win-win industry ecosystem.
HİZMETE ÖZEL - INTERNAL

[p3]
Lawrence koh
Chief Export Compliance Officer
ZTE Corporation
Lawrence.koh@zte.com.cn
+65 84999511 (Singapore)
+86 15768250208 (China)
HİZMETE ÖZEL - INTERNAL
